about.title: Chowchilla Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Chowchilla is a small, close-knit city, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when someone gets hurt on a wet floor, a broken sidewalk, or a poorly lit parking area near Robertson Boulevard or Trinity Avenue. Whether the fall happened at a local business, an apartment building, or on public property, California law requires the owner to have known or reasonably should have known about the hazard before they can be held responsible. That's why documenting exactly what caused the fall matters so much here — a cracked step, a spill left unattended, a torn mat. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free connection service that matches injured Chowchilla residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property conditions, pull any available surveillance footage, and help you understand your options. There's no cost to find out where you stand, and no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Chowchilla Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance records, prior complaints, or inspection logs to establish this.

items.title: Acting Before Video Disappears
items.desc: Many Chowchilla businesses and apartment complexes only retain surveillance footage for a short window. Preserving that video quickly can be critical to showing exactly how and why the fall happened.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault can reduce the amount recovered. An attorney can help present the facts fairly on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Chowchilla?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If your fall happened on government-owned property, such as a city sidewalk or public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. Speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later helps protect your options.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my own fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so you may still be able to recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is something an attorney can help evaluate based on the specific circumstances.

items.question: I fell at a store off SR-99 near Chowchilla — what should I do first?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the hazard, note the time and weather conditions, and ask if an incident report was filed with the store. Surveillance cameras at many properties along SR-99 and Robertson Boulevard only hold footage for a limited time, so having an attorney request preservation of that video promptly can be important.
